paper_metadata.title: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations for financial risk analytics: scenario generation for equity, rate, and credit risk factors

summary: The paper presents four gate-based quantum Monte Carlo / QAE circuit constructions for financial risk analytics: equity binomial trees, interest-rate trinomial trees, structural credit risk, and reduced-form credit survival. It reports simulator-based convergence results, with the main resource estimates reaching roughly 1,200 input qubits for realistic scenarios and circuit depth on the order of 10^8 for n=14 output qubits, but it does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: End-to-end quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation circuit for equity risk factors using a binomial tree to generate stock-price scenarios and estimate probabilities of maximum/minimum outcomes.

algorithm.variant: QAE with phase estimation and Grover-style amplitude amplification

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One risk-factor qubit per timestep encodes down/up moves in a binomial tree; one risk-measure qubit encodes the target probability; output register used for phase estimation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate probabilities P(S_max)=q^m and P(S_min)=(1-q)^m for the terminal stock-price distribution generated by a geometric Brownian motion discretized with a binomial tree.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: m-2 for Mmax/Mmin in simplest form

problem_instance.description: Equity price scenario generation for a single stock under geometric Brownian motion, discretized with a binomial tree.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic stochastic process; no market dataset used.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated runs on a zero-noise simulator; convergence shown for n=1..9 output qubits and 10,000-shot histograms for n=4.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure output register, map measured integer z to theta and then to probability p via p=sin^2(z*pi/2^n).

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: monotonic convergence of estimated probability toward expected value as n increases

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate P(A_T <= D_T), the probability of default in a Merton-style structural credit model.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Counting and state-selection logic; OR over default states to flip the risk-measure qubit.
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At least 1 ancilla for counting subcircuits; paper notes 3 count qubits and 2 state qubits

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One risk-factor qubit per timestep encodes survival/default; one risk-measure qubit encodes survival probability at T; default propagation is enforced by controlled rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate P(T) = exp(-sum delta t / T_def), equivalently the survival probability at time T, with default represented by the complement.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Controlled rotation ensures once default occurs, later timesteps remain default.

experiments.description: Reduced-form credit risk scenario generation using a Poisson-process survival model discretized into a quantum circuit, with survival probability encoded by repeated Ry rotations and a controlled default propagation gate.

algorithm.variant: QAE with phase estimation and Grover-style amplitude amplification

key_results: Paper reports m=6 timesteps and qdef=2% for the reduced-form model.
Expected survival probability at T is (1-qdef)^m.
